source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade / Downgrade HIB-CPLD firmware by Redfish when system is off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; assumes HIB-CPLD from Items/Script and fails to address the Procedure's explicit FPGA operation, so its image and inventory advice is not target-safe.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; correctly withholds unsafe Redfish execution but focuses on missing contracts more than the destructive target contradiction.

historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: The archived sequence-900 draft detected the conflict but is non-counting history; the exact row was independently reassessed.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The approved target-preservation rule forbids automatically replacing a named CPLD with FPGA, but its enumerated ruling does not explicitly adjudicate BMC-00022; Rule 1 therefore requires preserving both texts and seeking an engineer decision.

original_test_intent: The Items and linked script indicate a host-off HIB-CPLD Redfish upgrade/downgrade with one BMC reset, while the Procedure explicitly commands FPGA firmware. Until the library owner selects the authoritative component, the destructive test purpose is internally contradictory.
original_method: The row uses generic Immediate PATCH, binary POST and FirmwareInventory GET requests with no component selector, embedded default credentials and disabled TLS verification. That generic path cannot resolve whether the image is intended for HIB-CPLD or FPGA.
manual_activity: The library/platform owner must adjudicate the component identity. After that decision, an authorized engineer must approve the corrected image, Redfish route, single-reset semantics and recovery; no agent may infer the target from filename, DeepSeek or neighboring cases.
required_inputs: explicit engineer ruling selecting HIB-CPLD or FPGA for this exact code
aligned device/board inventory, current/target versions and signed images
component-specific Redfish selector/action, task and inventory mapping
secure authentication, trusted TLS, stable power and target-specific recovery
safety_requirements: Do not upload any image while Items/Script identify HIB-CPLD and Procedure identifies FPGA; choosing either interpretation could program the wrong device.
Do not use the generic UpdateService POST unless the approved vendor contract proves an immutable component selector or image-manifest binding.
Never execute the literal `root:0penBmc` URL or `curl -k`; unsafe authentication does not become acceptable after target correction.
Preserve all source fields and record the correction only in the review/decision layer; do not overwrite the Master row.
After correction, run one approved direction/reset at a time and never retry automatically on ambiguity or failure.
agent_execution_scope: While the target remains unresolved, perform no PATCH, POST, reset or power action; retain the conflicting texts and prepare the exact question for engineering ownership.
After an explicit decision, rediscover the component-bound service and validate image-to-device and inventory mappings before any execution plan is considered.
Collect evidence and report facts only; do not declare a DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Decide whether BMC-00022 is an HIB-CPLD or FPGA update and approve the corrected procedure/coverage without changing the preserved source.
Approve the selected device, images, API/reset/recovery contract and later issue direction-specific verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek's HIB-CPLD flow follows Items and Script but silently overrides the Procedure's FPGA instruction. Generic POST and FirmwareInventory evidence cannot prove which component would be written.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No firmware command is authorized. After an engineer target decision, use a secure vendor-advertised action explicitly bound to that device and retain the other interpretation as uncovered source conflict history.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: HIB-CPLD Items/Script, FPGA Procedure, source PATCH/POST/GET, host-off state, one-BMC-reset criterion and 10/30-minute values remain verbatim evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: First adjudicate and document the authoritative component. Then bind a signed image to its exact board/inventory member, use a component-specific secure Redfish action, observe the approved single-reset activation and verify target-specific plus platform health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the explicitly selected HIB-CPLD or FPGA on the confirmed platform.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record selected device/board/image, BMC/Redfish schema, client/CA and recovery-tool revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor update, activation and recovery documentation for the selected programmable device.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an authoritative component decision and immutable routing before replacing unsafe authentication and assumed service behavior.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Prevents a successful transaction against the wrong device from being accepted; the non-selected target remains untested unless covered separately.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer decision and target-specific vendor contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: HIB-CPLD and FPGA are not interchangeable targets, images or recovery domains.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may define versions and tools only after engineering resolves the Master target contradiction. A project override cannot silently convert HIB-CPLD to FPGA or claim equivalent coverage without the explicit decision, reason and uncovered-target record.
expected_evidence: signed engineer decision naming one authoritative component and preserving the conflicting Master text
aligned device/board/version/image matrix with hashes and signatures
component-bound action, selector, inventory mapping and redacted completion transcript
selected-target version and affected link/platform health
target-specific recovery readiness and engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script name HIB-CPLD, but the Procedure explicitly says FPGA firmware. The generic POST and generic FirmwareInventory query contain no component selector that could disambiguate the destructive target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is not merely a missing image or Project SPEC value: the hardware destination and recovery domain conflict inside the source. Executing either interpretation risks programming the wrong device, so execution remains BLOCKED until an engineer resolves the target.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes its PARTIAL conclusion to BLOCKED because its HIB-CPLD assumption is an unauthorized source rewrite and its generic API cannot prove routing.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains BLOCKED but identifies the HIB-CPLD-versus-FPGA contradiction—not ordinary missing inputs—as the irreducible reason.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms the target conflict and adds explicit preservation, engineer-decision and uncovered-target requirements.

review_improvement: Separates a genuine destructive-target contradiction from ordinary readiness gaps and prevents DeepSeek's title-based assumption from becoming an unauthorized Master correction.
independent_technical_reasoning: Firmware image compatibility and recovery are component-specific. Because the only write path is generic and the source names two different programmable devices, neither a successful HTTP response nor FirmwareInventory can establish safe target selection. This meets the V3.1 narrow BLOCKED condition until engineering adjudicates HIB-CPLD versus FPGA.
